subject: End-to-end latency qualification — summary and risk register
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Eli Matthews <eli@brightleaf.com>
Cc: Priya Nair <priya@brightleaf.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-11T16:08:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: BrightLeaf latency targets + next steps

Hi Eli / Priya — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

1) Targets we discussed
   - p95 E2E (user request → first token): 120 ms target (current provider ~160 ms)
   - p99 E2E: 420–500 ms acceptable target (current provider ~820 ms)

2) Traffic profile you shared
   - Peak concurrent sessions: 35–40 (burst to 60 for promotions)
   - Typical request length: 80–220 tokens (median ~140)
   - Streaming transcripts turned on for 100% of requests (low-latency partial outputs matter)

3) Immediate asks from BrightLeaf (as I heard them):
   - A: Can Redwood hit p95/p99 at production concurrency with streaming on?
   - B: Test harness and example workload (you offered telemetry export)
   - C: Short list of mitigations we can apply in a PoC (caching, batching, model variant)

Next steps (proposed):
  - BrightLeaf: share the anonymized telemetry CSV and the handshake test account (Eli) — target: EOD Thu 5/13
  - Redwood (Ben + Naomi): produce an SLO risk register + PoC plan and quick-win checklist — target: Mon 5/17
  - Schedule an engineering deep-dive (90m) the week of 5/24 to run through test harness and streaming concurrency knobs

Attached: placeholder for telemetry (you said you'd export), and I attached a blank risk register for us to iterate.

If any of that is off, flag it here. Otherwise I’ll tee up the deep-dive invite once we have telemetry.

Cheers,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0189
Redwood Inference

From: Eli Matthews <eli@brightleaf.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Nair <priya@brightleaf.com>
Date: 2027-05-12T09:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: BrightLeaf latency targets + next steps

Thanks Jordan — concise and accurate. A few clarifications and the telemetry export attached.

Clarifications from our infra team:
 - The current provider (IncumbentAI) median is ~145 ms; p95 ~160 ms; p99 ~820 ms (we think p99 spike is due to long-tail DB lookups in our layer).
 - Concurrency: steady 30–35, 1–2 short bursts/day to 55–60. Most bursts last <120s.
 - Streaming: yes, we need partial transcript streaming to the client (websocket) and cannot buffer for full completion in production.

Constraints:
 - TLS termination is in our VPC (we can proxy).
 - Data retention / auditing: we need audit logs for inference calls for SOC-related review (we will evaluate Redwood Private later).

Attached: brightleaf-current-telemetry-20270510.csv (anonymized request log; columns: ts, seq_len, latency_first_byte_ms, total_latency_ms, model, endpoint)

We’ll share an engineer for the deep-dive if you want (Priya can coordinate).

—Eli
Eli Matthews, Head of Platform | BrightLeaf
eli@brightleaf.com | +1 617-555-0113

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Eli Matthews <eli@brightleaf.com>
Cc: Priya Nair <priya@brightleaf.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-13T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: BrightLeaf latency targets + next steps

Appreciate the telemetry, Eli — looked through the CSV and sketched initial observations. High-level notes for the risk register: 

Observations from telemetry (quick scan):
 - There are two distinct latency modes: streaming-enabled requests (slightly higher first-byte latency) and non-streaming completions.
 - A non-trivial tail (>99.5th) aligns with spikes in backend DB enrichment calls (internal to BrightLeaf).

Potential quick wins for PoC (short checklist):
 1) Prefix/KV caching: enable prefix cache for repeated prompts (expect ~15–25% p95 improvement for repeated flows).
 2) Streaming concurrency tuning: pre-warm pool capacity and increase per-instance concurrency to support ~40 sessions with streaming enabled; this reduces queuing tail.
 3) Per-request early partial flush: prioritize first-token emission path in runtime (small runtime config tweak we can demo).
 4) Traffic shaping on burst windows: graceful shedding of non-critical background enrichment at ingress (coordination with your infra).

Open risks / unknowns (for the register):
 - Internal DB enrichment latency at BrightLeaf — if that remains in-path, p99 will be dominated by backend and not Redwood.
 - TLS proxy path and additional hop risk: ensure we can measure e2e from client edge to token emission.

I’ll put these into the risk register and attach a short-runbook for the PoC config. Naomi — can you prepare a mini-POC plan (3-phase: smoke, scaled run, streaming soak) and timing?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Sr. Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Attachment referenced: redwood-poc-runbook-mini-20270513.md (see drive link)
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Priya Nair <priya@brightleaf.com>
Date: 2027-05-14T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: BrightLeaf latency targets + next steps

Hi Eli / team — schedule lookahead and concrete asks from Redwood for the deep-dive: 

1) What we need from BrightLeaf before the deep-dive (please upload to the shared Drive or drop in the HubSpot record):
   - Representative request trace (one anonymized full flow that includes DB enrichment call timing)
   - Expected peak-burst windows (date/times typical) and one example replay window
   - Confirmation that we can run a 24–48h soak with production-like traffic to validate p99 stability

2) Proposed 90m deep-dive agenda (we’ll send calendar invites once you confirm availability):
   - 0–15m: Goals and success criteria (Jordan)
   - 15–45m: Telemetry walkthrough and trace dissection (BrightLeaf + Ben)
   - 45–75m: PoC plan and runtime knobs (Naomi) — batching, prefix caching, streaming concurrency, model variant mapping
   - 75–90m: Q&A and immediate action items (owners & due dates)

3) PoC timeline (draft)
   - Week 1: smoke tests and baseline comparison (incumbent vs Redwood hosted)
   - Week 2: scaled run with streaming concurrency enabled; capture p95/p99 envelopes
   - Week 3: soak and regression checks; finalize SLO guidance and draft contract appendix

If you’re ok with this we’ll (a) update the risk register with Ben’s notes and your telemetry-derived items, (b) schedule the deep-dive, and (c) prepare a short test harness (link below) you can run from your env to reproduce our baseline.

Test harness: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c-redwood-runbook-view
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/company/brightleaf

Thanks — Naomi
